title: The secret handshake
kid: The video server and {yours} do a secret handshake before the film starts. The server shows its ID card with a gold stamp, and both sides mix colours so they get the same lock colour. After that, every parcel travels locked.
nerd: TLS 1.3, one round trip: the ClientHello carries SNI and an X25519 share g^a; the ServerHello answers with g^b. Both compute g^ab and derive keys with HKDF. Then, already encrypted, the server sends its certificate chain (leaf → intermediate, anchored at a root in the trust store; name and dates checked) and a CertificateVerify signature that proves it owns the certificate’s key. Records are then protected with AEAD (AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305), RFC 8446.

describe.kid: A road links {yours} and the video server. The first card shows an ID card and a trusted stamp book. The second card shows paint pots mixing on both sides. A crow watches only the public mixes, pale peach and lime. Then a lock clicks onto the parcel, and the locked parcel travels down the road.
describe.nerd: The cards depict TLS 1.3 from the client endpoint. The paint equations show the key agreement first; the identity card then shows certificate validation, sent already encrypted. The crow sees the public shares on the wire, never the secrets or the certificate. Then the parcel becomes an encrypted record and moves to the server.

cdn.title: The server proves who it is
cdn.kid: The video server shows its ID card with a gold stamp. It mixes its secret colour too, so it gets the very same lock colour as {yours}. Then it sends video parcels that only the two ends can open.
cdn.nerd: At the server endpoint, TLS terminates: the server’s X25519 secret combines with the client’s public share to derive the same traffic keys. Then, already encrypted, it sends its certificate for video.example and a CertificateVerify signature that proves it holds the certificate’s key. Records leave as authenticated ciphertext under the chosen TLS 1.3 cipher suite.

describe.kid: The video server is highlighted at the end of the road. It shows its stamped ID card, mixes its paint with the mix from {yours}, and ends with the same lock colour. The crow can watch the pale mixtures. After the lock appears, the parcel travels as a locked box that only the two ends can open.
describe.nerd: At the server endpoint, the cards show ECDHE as paint and then the certificate chain. The server contributes its public share and derives matching traffic keys. The crow on the wire can see the server name and the public values, not the certificate, which is already encrypted. After that, only authenticated ciphertext records move as locked parcels.

sealed.title: Locked on the way
sealed.kid: Step by step: 1. The video server shows its ID to {yours}. 2. Each side mixes in a secret colour and swaps only the mix. 3. Both get the same colour, and it locks the parcel. {hop} just carries it. Like the crow, it sees only the mixes and a locked box.
sealed.nerd: At {hop}, TLS is sealed end to end: 1. ECDHE agrees a key, 2. the server proves itself with its certificate and a CertificateVerify signature, both already encrypted, 3. AEAD seals every record. The hop forwards lower-layer headers; it may observe the ClientHello’s server name (SNI, unless Encrypted Client Hello is used) and the two ECDHE public shares, but not the certificate (encrypted in TLS 1.3), the HTTP request or the keys.

describe.kid: A middle stop sits on the road while {yours} and the server are at the ends. Card 1 shows the ID check and card 2 the paint mixing, and the crow watches the pale public mixes. When the lock appears, the parcel’s face turns into scribbles. The stop just carries the locked parcel onward.
describe.nerd: This non-endpoint view shows TLS sealed above the hop. The ECDHE shares and the server name are visible on the wire; the certificate is already encrypted. The device you are at only forwards lower-layer packets. Once records are protected, the moving parcel is locked and scrambled as ciphertext, not readable HTTP.
